question: Show all pairs of entertainers and customers who each have up to three style strengths or preferences, where the first and second style preferences of the customers match the first and second style strengths of the entertainers (or in reverse order). Only return the entertainer’s stage name and the customer’s last name
sql:
-- Fix: use the correct ROW_NUMBER ordering
WITH ent_ranked AS (
    SELECT EntertainerID, StyleID, StyleStrength,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY EntertainerID ORDER BY StyleStrength DESC, StyleID ASC) as rn
    FROM Entertainer_Styles
),
ent_top2 AS (
    SELECT EntertainerID,
           MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN StyleID END) as ent_style_1,
           MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 2 THEN StyleID END) as ent_style_2
    FROM ent_ranked
    GROUP BY EntertainerID
),
cust_prefs AS (
    SELECT CustomerID,
           MAX(CASE WHEN PreferenceSeq = 1 THEN StyleID END) as cust_style_1,
           MAX(CASE WHEN PreferenceSeq = 2 THEN StyleID END) as cust_style_2
    FROM Musical_Preferences
    GROUP BY CustomerID
),
ent_valid AS (
    SELECT EntertainerID
    FROM Entertainer_Styles
    GROUP BY EntertainerID
    HAVING COUNT(*) <= 3
),
cust_valid AS (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM Musical_Preferences
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(*) <= 3
)
SELECT e.EntStageName, c.CustLastName
FROM ent_valid ev
JOIN ent_top2 et ON ev.EntertainerID = et.EntertainerID
JOIN cust_valid cv ON 1=1
JOIN cust_prefs cp ON cv.CustomerID = cp.CustomerID
JOIN Entertainers e ON ev.EntertainerID = e.EntertainerID
JOIN Customers c ON cv.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE 
    (cp.cust_style_1 = et.ent_style_1 AND cp.cust_style_2 = et.ent_style_2)
    OR
    (cp.cust_style_1 = et.ent_style_2 AND cp.cust_style_2 = et.ent_style_1)
ORDER BY e.EntStageName, c.CustLastName
